correctness.rationale: After eventual ordering, a fixed-proportion prime isolates the top factorial unless the top two slopes coincide. Cancelling that pair and repeating the argument forces the bottom two slopes to coincide. The remaining fixed-length block polynomial is square-valued for every large integer; the proved finite-difference lemma turns this into a polynomial square. Simple-root matching then forces both gaps to equal one, and the two residual linear factors to be rational-square associates. Clearing denominators gives the coprime-square normal form; direct factorial algebra proves the converse.
